utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We're sorry about the delay in starting. The reason for that is simply that the document that has been filed is filed ex parte, and it was our prima facie view that the opposite party may be interested in the content, and we were trying to lift the ex parte and confidential aspect of it but without success. So you'll have to accept, as the Prosecution, that the condition of the accused as mentioned in the document justifies his absence from court according to -- I think the part of the document that can be discussed, it is for 10 days that he will be absent, starting from the 10th of May, which means that we will schedule the case now from 10 days after the 10th of May. Have I made a mistake? Shouldn't we have been in private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I don't think the Court has disclosed anything that can't be in public session, frankly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. So that's the situation. The situation is that we will not have the accused here for 10 days, starting from the 10th, so we will not be able to sit for those days. The 10th day obviously ends on the 20th, which is a Saturday. I imagine the Prosecution would be able to schedule a witness for the 22nd, which is the Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You will be able to. Now, 10 days was the outside time. It's seven to 10 days. Now, if he recovers within the 10 days, I don't know how you schedule a witness all of a sudden. It said seven to 10 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it's -- we need several days lead-time. Obviously, we're canceling now all the witnesses for next week. So in order to put a witness back on, we need several days lead-time to make arrangements. So it seems to me that it's unlikely that is going to be possible given the information that the Court has provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. That's quite understandable. Having said that, the Chamber is concerned to use these days profitably somehow, and it was the view of -- at least my view, I haven't even discussed it with the other Judges yet, that maybe in the coming week we could, both parties and the Chamber, discuss concretely around -- can we move into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Back to scheduling. Shall we then postpone definitely to the 22nd, or postpone without a date?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it would be our preference to postpone definitely to the 22nd. I did have one question about the medical report. It's my understanding from a conversation with Defence counsel that they did not receive it either. So is that the way it's going to be left, that it's the Trial Chamber that receives it and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No. The cover sheet says "Ex Parte, Confidential," and it mentions the Defence at the bottom. It is filed by Registry. So the assumption was that Defence has a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: They indicated to me this morning that they had not received a copy. So I don't know if that's...

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, we've just received it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm told it's being filed as we speak, so they should be able to get a copy. Okay. Then we postpone until the 22nd of May. Is that it? Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 22nd day of May, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.26 a.m.,
